notes: Plan-only evals grade strict direct review for the deliver controllers. Each operation resolves once into a retained ResolvedProject; refusal is fatal and no policy is defaulted or inferred. Every operation ends in exactly one result object. Case 4 is a review-ship pipeline case of a paired trial corpus, and it makes no Codex call because the fixture's code review is unsupported. Case 5 grades the one fresh retry of a failed review call: a slice whose retry succeeds completes the review, and a slice that fails twice is reported while the other slices' results stand.

evals.name: plan-review-direct-command-and-capability
evals.prompt: A deliver controller dispatches plan-review with the absolute plan path /work/wt/.git/deliver/plan.md (task files beside it) and the acceptance criteria as JSON, for issue #42 in the worktree /work/wt. capabilities.review.plan is available, and bindings.commands[review_id].argv is ["codex-companion","task","--fresh","--reviewer","plan-review"]. Plan-only: explain selection, binding shape, packet, direct invocation, validation, failure handling, and the returned result.
evals.expected_output: Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject and select bindings.workflow.review.plan, capabilities.review.plan, and bindings.commands[review_id]; a refusal is fatal. blocked stops with its reason and repair ID; unsupported makes no Codex call and returns to the caller with no result. Classify the authored argv: basename codex-companion, subcommand task, --reviewer plan-review matching the running operation, optional --fresh and no other token make it the one supported shape; any other argv, bare ["codex"] included, is a binding shape error naming the expected form codex-companion task [--fresh] --reviewer <op> and its cause, with no Codex call and no retry. Stop before packet construction when the plan path is missing, relative or unreadable. The packet carries the issue reference, the caller's acceptance criteria, the plan root with its task files, the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md chain, bindings.paths.hints and the matching standards, with verification entries as context only. Invoke the base argv/cwd/env plus `--model gpt-6-astra --effort xhigh --cwd <absolute-worktree> --json`, sending the packet on stdin with no positional argument, in the foreground. Require exit 0 and exactly one JSON object with status 0, empty touchedFiles, runtime.model gpt-6-astra, runtime.reasoningEffort xhigh and a non-empty rawOutput before the Blocking / Should fix / Discussion headings establish Codex. Return the validated result unmodified as one object: Blocking mapped to critical, Should fix to important, Discussion to minor, verdict pass when Blocking and Should fix are both None. Every failure (daemon, slot or capacity rejection, runtime failure, malformed payload, schema failure) gets one fresh retry of the same packet and never another reviewer; a second failure is returned as available: false with its failure class and the verbatim message. The raw transcript is not stored.

evals.expected_output: Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject and select bindings.workflow.review.code, capabilities.review.code, and bindings.commands[review_id]; a refusal is fatal. blocked stops with its reason and repair ID; unsupported makes no Codex call and returns to the caller with no result. Run the size pre-flight with the resolved artifact paths: 44 files split into three slices of 20, 20 and 4 in emitted order, dispatched together as background jobs of one shell command that waits for them all with the scoped-review statement and the selected paths with changed lines, each path collected by exactly one `git diff <base>..<head> -- ':(literal)<path>'`. evals.name: native-diff-review-before-ship
evals.prompt:
Use the `codex-collaboration` skill's `diff-review` on the existing linked worktree branch `worktree-issue-3-rename-flag` (find it with `git worktree list`), over `main...worktree-issue-3-rename-flag`.

Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject. A resolver refusal is fatal and values are never defaulted or inferred. You are the calling controller: when the operation hands the review back to your native route, review that diff yourself in this session, read-only, and print the findings under Critical, Important and Minor.

**Stop after the review.** Do not edit, commit, push or merge anything.
evals.expected_output: The run routes capabilities.review.code (unsupported in the fixture) to no Codex call, says so, and reviews the range natively under the three severity sections Critical, Important and Minor. Nothing is edited, committed, pushed or merged.

asserts.name: nothing was pushed
asserts.shell: [ "$(git -C "$ORIGIN" for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname)')" = "$ORIGIN_REFS" ] || fail "origin's refs changed since setup despite the stop: $(git -C "$ORIGIN" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' | tr '\n' ' ')"

asserts.name: local and origin main are unchanged
asserts.shell: { [ "$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse main)" = "$BASE_MAIN" ] && [ "$(git -C "$ORIGIN" rev-parse main)" = "$BASE_MAIN" ] && git -C "$REPO" diff --quiet "$BASE_MAIN" -- && [ -z "$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)" ]; } || fail "main moved or the base checkout was edited: $(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | tr '\n' ' ')"

asserts.name: the branch still carries the implementation
asserts.shell: { [ -n "$PRE_WT_HEAD" ] && [ "$(git -C "$PRE_WT" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$PRE_WT_HEAD" ]; } || { fail "worktree-issue-3-rename-flag moved off its setup tip"; exit 1; }; commits_touch "$PRE_WT" tinytask

asserts.name: the worktree is left exactly as committed
asserts.shell: { [ -n "$PRE_WT_HEAD" ] && git -C "$PRE_WT" diff --quiet "$PRE_WT_HEAD" -- && [ -z "$(git -C "$PRE_WT" status --porcelain)" ]; } || fail "the review changed $PRE_WT since setup"

asserts.name: the run names the native route for the unsupported capability
the run prints the Critical, Important and Minor sections
asserts.shell: out_matches '^[[:space:]#*_-]*critical([[:space:]]*\(must fix\))?[[:space:]*_:]*$' && out_matches '^[[:space:]#*_-]*important([[:space:]]*\(should fix\))?[[:space:]*_:]*$' && out_matches '^[[:space:]#*_-]*minor[[:space:]*_:]*$' && out_matches 'README|test_cli|cli\.py'

evals.name: diff-review-failed-slice-retried-once
evals.prompt: A controller dispatches diff-review and the range has 44 product files. Slice 1 returns one Important finding. Slice 2's first call returns companion exit 1 with payload status 1 and prose with no finding headings. In the first part, any further call for slice 2 with the same packet returns a valid result with None. in every section, and slice 3 returns None. in every section. In the second part, every call for slice 2 fails the same way, and slice 3 returns one Minor finding. Plan-only: explain whether slice 2 is called again, which slices run, and the one returned object for each part.
evals.expected_output: Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject and select bindings.workflow.review.code, capabilities.review.code, and bindings.commands[review_id]; a refusal is fatal. Run the size pre-flight: 44 files split into three slices of 20, 20 and 4 in emitted order, dispatched together as background jobs of one shell command that waits for them all. Invoke the base argv/cwd/env plus `--model gpt-6-astra --effort xhigh --cwd <absolute-worktree> --json` with the packet on stdin, and require exit 0 and exactly one JSON object with status 0, empty touchedFiles, runtime.model gpt-6-astra, runtime.reasoningEffort xhigh, a non-empty rawOutput and the Critical / Important / Minor headings. Slice 2's first call is a failed run, so it gets one fresh retry of the same packet in its own mktemp -d directory, never another reviewer and never a third call; slice 3 ran beside it and is not called again. First part: the retry validates and the review is complete: return available: true, verdict: findings, slice 1's finding as important, and a raw_summary of `scope: 3 slices over 44 product files`, base and head SHAs and three slice <i>: lines, with no failed slices line. Second part: the retry fails too, and slice 3's result stands; return available: false, verdict: findings, findings holding slice 1's important finding then slice 3's minor finding, and a raw_summary whose slice 2 line gives the failure class and the verbatim message (the payload error, else stderr), followed by `failed slices: 2`. The completed slices' lines and findings stay in the result, so a relaunch need only re-review slice 2. A binding shape error is never retried.
